text: Butt-coupling light from a standard single-mode fiber directly into a 450x220 nm silicon waveguide (no mode converter) is catastrophic because of mode-size mismatch. Approximately what is this direct-coupling loss, and what is the standard fix?
choices: ~3 dB; simply increase the laser power
~22 dB; use an inverse taper (~1-2 dB) or a grating coupler (~0.5-1.5 dB)
explanation: The ~10 um fiber mode overlaps very poorly with the sub-micron silicon mode, giving about 22 dB loss; inverse tapers (spot-size converters) or grating couplers restore this to 1-2 dB or 0.5-1.5 dB. Raising laser power does not recover coupling efficiency, a longer fiber is irrelevant, and 1 dB or 0.18 dB grossly understate the mismatch penalty.
